name: Bismarck
description: Bismarck is a Swedish three-player trick-taking game where players score based on the number of tricks they win compared to a 'quota.' Over 12 deals, each player must play each of four different contracts exactly once as forehand: Sang (no trumps, win tricks), Pass (no trumps, avoid tricks), Spader (spades trump), and Valfri (choose your trump suit). Similar to the Polish game Mizerka.

history.origins: The first known description of Bismarck appeared in 1944 in Sweden. According to Sten Helmfrid (Kartofilen, July 2024), the game was likely named after the famous German battleship Bismarck, which was sunk in 1941 â€” making this a WW2-era card game.
timeline: 1941: Battleship Bismarck sunk â€” likely inspiration for the game's name.
1944: First known published rules of the card game appear in Sweden.
Late 20th century: Spreads to Britain, Finland, Portugal, and Estonia.
Present: Played in multiple variants across Northern and Western Europe.
history.cultural: A distinctively Scandinavian card game that reflects the Northern European love of structured trick-taking games with strategic depth.
history.evolution: Bismarck belongs to the 'quota whist' family where players score based on deviation from a target number of tricks. It shares DNA with Mizerka (Poland) and other European three-player trick-taking games. The compulsory contract rotation system ensures variety across a full game.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck, no Jokers. Cards rank A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2.
setup.dealing: Dealer shuffles; player to dealer's right cuts. Dealer deals the top 4 cards face-up on the table, then deals the remaining 48 cards face-down to the three players (16 each). Forehand (left of dealer) picks up the 4 face-up cards (total 20 cards) and discards any 4 face-down.
setup.equipment: 52-card deck. Score sheet with grid (rows: players, columns: contracts).

rules.objective: Over 12 deals (each player is forehand 4 times), score the highest cumulative total by managing your tricks relative to your quota.
rules.gameplay: Forehand leads to the first trick. Any card may be led. Players must follow suit if possible; if void, may play any card. With trumps the trick is won by the highest trump; with no trumps, by the highest card of the led suit. There is no obligation to beat or to overtrump. The winner of each trick leads to the next. After 16 tricks, players are scored against their quota for the chosen contract.
keyRules: Forehand sees 4 face-up cards BEFORE choosing their contract â€” critical information for decision-making.
Forehand picks up the 4 face-up cards and discards 4, keeping 16 for play.
Each contract must be used exactly once per player over 12 deals.
16 tricks per deal (3 players Ã— 16 cards Ã· 3? No â€” 48 cards Ã· 3 = 16 each, so 16 tricks).
Zero-sum scoring: all three scores always add to zero.

strategy.basic: As forehand, evaluate the 4 face-up cards carefully before choosing your contract. With many high cards and a strong suit, choose Sang or a trump contract. With weak cards, choose Pass.
strategy.intermediate: Contract sequencing: save your most flexible contract (Valfri) for last so you can adapt to your hand. Spader should be chosen when you naturally have good spades. Don't waste Valfri on spades if you haven't played Spader yet.
strategy.advanced: In Sang (no-trump, win tricks), count the cards: with 16 tricks, forehand needs 8 â€” exactly half. Lead your strong suits first to establish winners. In Pass (avoid tricks), avoid leading and duck with low cards. Discard strategy: when picking up the 4 face-up cards, discard to strengthen your chosen contract â€” void a suit for trump contracts, or shed high cards for Pass.
tips: The 4 face-up cards give forehand a 20-card hand â€” use the discard to tailor your hand perfectly.
Track the 4 discarded cards â€” they're out of play and affect trick counting.
In Pass, the quota is only 4 for forehand â€” try to take exactly 4 or fewer.
Contract sequencing over 12 deals is a meta-strategy: plan which contracts to play early vs. late.

scoring.description: Quota-based: +1 per trick over quota, -1 per trick under. Zero-sum across 3 players. Tracked on a grid with cumulative totals.
scoring.winCondition: Highest cumulative score after all 12 deals.

synthesis.shortDescription: A Swedish three-player trick-taking game named after the famous battleship. Over 12 deals, each player must play four different contracts â€” no trumps (win or avoid), spades trump, or choose your trump. Score by beating your trick quota. The face-up cards give forehand crucial information before committing.
